text:
sophia: proposing an incremental vertical-slicing approach for the inference stack. idea is to peel feature domains top-to-bottom (api surface -> controller -> runtime slice) instead of big horizontal cuts. goal: lower blast radius, easier rollbacks, clear runtime contracts.
sophia: example slice = "routing + prefix-cache + model-variant" for a single product flow. each slice owns its KV keys + telemetry.
matt: curious — how do we avoid duplicated logic across slices? sounds like risk of code drift.
sophia: good point. plan is a small shared lib for primitives (auth, metrics, retry), but no shared business logic. contract tests + CI enforce parity.
raj: what's migration signal? how do we know a slice is safe to flip primary traffic to?
sophia: we use canary windows + success metrics: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, unit-cost delta, and quality regressions from the eval harness. target: 2% cost variance and <1% quality drift.
olivia: do we need new infra components to route by slice? or can we reuse request-router with route headers?
sophia: reuse router, add a lightweight slice header (X-Runtime-Slice) and a server-side router policy. no global load-balancer changes.
luis: I worry about stateful pieces (session KV, prefix cache). ownership transfer is messy. any notes on cache migration?
sophia: migrate with dual-write for prefix cache during canary, then switch read path. we'll keep consistent keys and version pinning in cache metadata. plan includes a small migration shim:
```
# shim pseudo
if request.headers["X-Slice-Version"] == "v2":
  write(cache_v2, key, value)
  read_prefer = cache_v2
else:
  write(cache_v1, key, value)
  read_prefer = cache_v1
```
raj: dual-write is OK short-term but watch for double-cost. add sampling to measure overhead.
raj: also add a rollback guard that auto-fails to v1 if error-rate spike > threshold.
mat t: (typo) matt: +1 to rollback guard. who owns the circuit? eng-sre or slice team?
sophia: slice owning team owns the circuit while in canary; eng-sre owns global incident playbooks and the auto-fail mechanism.
infra-bot: deploy 17950-incr-slice-prototype started by sophia at 1795004000 :rocket:
luis: operational question — tracing needs to tag span with slice id and contract version. existing tracing schema supports an open field?
matt: yes we have span.tag("x.slice") available, but add contract_version as well. small change to tracing lib.
olivia: are we standardizing the runtime contract? can we draft a minimal interface (input proto + error model + metrics)?
sophia: draft here: 1) request proto = {customer_id, route, prompt, meta.version}, 2) response proto = {tokens, cost_meta, provenance}, 3) errors = {Transient, Dropped, ModelFallback} with canonical codes, 4) metrics = latency, token_count, cache_hit, quality_score.
raj: looks tight. add a test harness that runs golden prompts against old vs new slice and diffs quality_score. automatic flag to block rollout on >1% regression.
luis: perf testers — we'll need a synthetic workload generator for slice-level traffic to validate batching + latency SLOs. I'll own that.
infra-bot: perf-test: scheduled 1795005600 by luis
matt: timeline? rough phases please.
sophia: phase 0: design + contract (1 week). phase 1: prototype slice + unit tests (2 weeks). phase 2: canary dual-write + 10% traffic (2 weeks). phase 3: expand + monitor (3 weeks). phase 4: cutover and deprecate old path (1 week). overall ~9w.
olivia: blockers? dependencies?
sophia: contract tests + tracing lib change + small router policy flag. also need product to agree to evaluation prompts for quality gating.
raj: ok add RFC follow-up doc with explicit roll-forward/roll-back steps and dashboard links. I'll make a draft tomorrow.
luis: i'll add perf test scaffolding and a sample workload.
matt: +1. can we add a TODO to record cost impact per-slice in billing exports?
sophia: yes — add slice_id tag to cost events.
olivia: sounds good. thanks — this feels like a lower-risk path than a big horizontal split. :thumbsup:
sophia: thanks everyone. I'll open a formal RFC + checklist and ping eng-sre/product for alignment.
